chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Humayd ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who visited the House (Kaaba) before shaving [his head], he said: 'If he visited the House before shaving while knowing that it is not appropriate for him, then upon him is the blood of a sheep [fidya].'

key_terms.لاَ يَنْبَغِي: It is not appropriate / Not proper

ai.seo_question: What is the fidya penalty for a pilgrim who visits the Kaaba before shaving if they know it is improper?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the penalty of sacrificing a sheep (dam) is prescribed for a pilgrim who performs tawaf before shaving, provided they are aware that the order is significant. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the prescribed sequence of Hajj rituals, distinguishing between ignorance and deliberate deviation from the Sunnah. The requirement of 'knowledge' (ilm) in the condition underscores that the penalty applies specifically to those who knowingly disregard the proper order, reflecting a nuanced approach to ritual jurisprudence.
